# Overview {.unnumbered}

TinyTorch is a reference implementation for studying how a machine learning framework works. Its Python modules expose the operations that produce predictions, the graph that carries gradients, and the state that changes during training. This book accompanies that code in the spirit of the xv6 commentary: follow an execution path, explain the decisions it embodies, and check the explanation against the implementation.

Reading and building reinforce each other. A small trace makes a function understandable; a test checks whether that understanding survives an edge case; an integrated model shows whether the functions compose. The complete instructor solutions provide the reference for this process. NumPy supplies array storage and numerical operations, while TinyTorch implements the framework mechanisms around them.

| Part | Focus | What you build |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Part I: The Core Engine** | Memory, gradients, optimization | `Tensor`, activations, `Linear`, `CrossEntropyLoss`, `DataLoader`, autograd, `AdamW`, the training loop |
| **Part II: Deep Architectures** | Images, text, transformers | `Conv2d`, `BPETokenizer`, `Embedding`, `MultiHeadAttention`, `TransformerBlock`, a small GPT |
| **Part III: Systems & Acceleration** | Measuring and speeding up | Profiling, simulated INT8 quantization, compression, NumPy acceleration experiments, `KVCache`, benchmarking, the capstone |
| **Part IV: Extensions & Future Frontiers** | Beyond TinyTorch | A production bridge to kernels, compilers, and accelerators; no additional TinyTorch module |

: **The Four Parts of TinyTorch**: The implementation progresses from core operations to integrated experiments, followed by a production comparison. {#tbl-overview-parts tbl-colwidths="[28,24,48]"}

The chapters keep the reference implementation distinct from production comparisons. A simulated storage saving is identified as an estimate; a timing result comes from an experiment. Each part combines local tests with an integrated workload, so the reader can examine both an individual mechanism and the contract it must honor when another module calls it.
